key_insight: Decouple local visual fidelity from long-term temporal coherence by combining a Mode‑Seeking objective for short-range detail with a Mean‑Seeking (flow‑matching) objective for global consistency, implemented in a Decoupled Diffusion Transformer to enable fast long‑video generation.
problem_solved: Long-form video generation is bottlenecked by scarcity of diverse, high‑quality long videos: short-video data gives high fidelity but poor global coherence, while long-video data is limited; this paper solves how to leverage abundant short clips and limited long videos together.
method: Introduce a Decoupled Diffusion Transformer that separates local (mode‑seeking) and global (mean‑seeking) components within a unified representation.

Use a Mode‑Seeking objective (trained on abundant short videos) to preserve high‑fidelity, multimodal local content and a global Flow‑Matching head (supervised on long videos) for long‑range temporal consistency.
Train the two heads jointly but decoupled so local detail and long‑term structure are optimized with complementary losses, enabling faster and more scalable long‑video synthesis.
impact: Enables practitioners to generate coherent minutes‑long videos by leveraging plentiful short‑clip data for detail and limited long data for temporal structure, improving scalability and training efficiency for long video generative models.
